Framed by the Fed’s average-inflation-targeting shift announced by Powell in 2020 (a makeup strategy per Svensson and Woodford), this statement emphasizes continued accommodation at the zero lower bound via QE and forward guidance (Woodford; Bernanke) to support maximum employment, while signaling a gradual taper consistent with the Taylor principle (Clarida) rather than abrupt tightening. By characterizing inflation as largely transitory and stressing anchored expectations around 2 percent (the PCE goal), the Committee leans on credibility and communication to stabilize outcomes (Sargent; FOMC forward guidance). The explicit risk-management posture toward COVID-related uncertainty (the Brainard principle) makes the overall tone cautiously optimistic for growth and employment, with only mild hawkish nuance from the “taper soon” language.
